findings.claim: In ensure_loaded!, the lazy initialization `@loaded_locales ||= []` is not protected by LOAD_MUTEX. Concurrent threads read and write @loaded_locales without synchronization, which can cause lost writes or double loading.

verifier.reason: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62-65, ensure_loaded! lazily initializes @loaded_locales ||= [] (line 63) and checks @loaded_locales.include?(locale) (line 64) outside LOAD_MUTEX, which is only acquired inside load_locale (line 47). Concurrent threads can race on the unsynchronized initialization and reads against load_locale's mutation of @loaded_locales (line 58), risking lost writes and double loading locales.

findings.claim: Locales are not normalized to one type (Symbol or String) before the @loaded_locales include? check and insertion. Because :en != 'en', the same locale passed as a String and as a Symbol produces duplicate entries and redundant loads.

verifier.reason: Neither load_locale (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:46-60) nor ensure_loaded! (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62-65) normalizes locale to a Symbol or String before checking @loaded_locales.include?(locale) (lines 48, 64) or appending @loaded_locales << locale (line 58). Passing the same locale as both a Symbol (e.g., via config.locale at line 68) and a String causes @loaded_locales.include? to miss, redundantly reloads the locale's YAML files at line 56, and stores duplicate entries in @loaded_locales.

findings.claim: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks is included via send(:include, ...) even though include is public since Ruby 2.1.

verifier.reason: While config/initializers/i18n.rb:9 does use I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks), this is necessary rather than redundant because the repository explicitly supports and tests Ruby 2.0.0 (.travis.yml:23, README.md:28), where Module#include is private and calling .include directly would raise NoMethodError.

findings.claim: Backend classes are monkey-patched via send(:include), which is fragile across gem upgrades.

verifier.reason: While config/initializers/i18n.rb:5 and config/initializers/i18n.rb:9 call send(:include, ...) on I18n::Backend::Simple and I18n.backend.class, mixing in I18n::Backend::Pluralization and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks is the official documented extension API of the i18n gem (and the same pattern used by Rails' I18nRailtie), not fragile monkey-patching. Using send(:include, ...) is standard Ruby 2.0 compatibility (README.md:28) because Module#include was private prior to Ruby 2.1.

findings.claim: The custom fallback list drops the standard locale-ancestor fallbacks, so regional locales skip the matching base-language translations.

verifier.reason: In config/initializers/i18n.rb:12-24, FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash instead of I18n::Locale::Fallbacks and overrides [] to return only [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact, dropping standard locale-ancestor fallback resolution. Consequently, regional locales such as :pt_BR (which has a matching base locale in config/locales/server.pt.yml containing keys absent from config/locales/server.pt_BR.yml) and hyphenated regional tags skip base-language translations and fall back directly to SiteSetting.default_locale and :en.
